effect_size.excerpt: Total meat consumption (data not shown) did not show this significant positive association with RCC risk. Subjects in the highest quartile (compared with the lowest quartile) of consumption of high-fat spreads, red meat, dairy foods and cured meat had significantly increased risks: OR = 2·0 (95 % CI 1·4, 3·0), OR = 1·7 (95 % CI 1·0, 2·2), OR = 1·6 (95 % CI 1·1, 2·3) and OR = 1·8 (95 % CI 1·2, 2·7), respectively.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Increased risks were also associated with high-fat spreads, red and cured meats and dairy products (OR = 2·0, 95 % CI 1·4, 3·0, P trend = 0·001; OR = 1·7, 95 % CI 1·0, 2·2, P trend = 0·01; OR = 1·8, 95 % CI 1·2, 2·7, P trend = 0·02; OR = 1·6, 95 % CI 1·1, 2·3, P trend = 0·02, respectively).

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an overall effect size of 2.79 (95% CI: 1.24–6.32), suggesting that dairy is associated with a higher risk of renal cell carcinoma. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 78.48%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
